record.question: Which of the following is not correct regarding LEEP?
options: Tissue specimen is available for HPE
Suitable for CIN2 and CIN3 with adequate colposcopy
Can be done outpatient under LA
record.explanation: LEEP (loop electrosurgical excision procedure) is an excisional technique, so it yields a specimen for histopathological examination, it is performed as an outpatient procedure under local anaesthesia, and it is the appropriate treatment for CIN 2/CIN 3 when the lesion and squamocolumnar junction are fully visualised (adequate colposcopy). The incorrect statement is the one claiming follow-up with Pap smear: post-LEEP surveillance should be based on HPV testing (or HPV/cytology co-testing, typically at 6 months), because cytology alone is an inadequate and unreliable follow-up test after excision (low sensitivity and treatment-related cellular changes). Source check: printed page 8 of 'Obstetrics & Gynae Technical Subject Paper-IV', October 2022, item 82 matches the stem and all four options in the printed order A-D.
